answer: Use pairwise-bounded quadratic funding. Matching grants favor projects backed by many small donors, which tempts a farm to split one wallet into hundreds. So the bonus each pair of donors adds is capped and shrinks the more often those two back the same projects. Clones that always move together soon add almost nothing. Real neighbors funding a wharf repair also back scattered other causes, so their overlap stays low; a whisper campaign of clones makes only a small ripple in the match.
